findings: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::ssrf: user-supplied host/port are connected to with no allowlist or private/link-local blocking, and connection errors are returned to the caller as a scan oracle

packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::ssrf / internal network probing: user-supplied host+port are connected to unvalidated, and testconnection returns the raw connection error to the caller as an oracle

packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::ssrf / internal port scanning: user-supplied host+port are connected to with no allowlist, and raw driver errors are returned to the caller, making the backend an oracle for the internal network

packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::tls certificate validation disabled (`rejectunauthorized: false`) when sslenabled is set, so "ssl on" gives no mitm protection for datasource credentials or query results

packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::tls certificate verification is disabled for all datasource connections (`rejectunauthorized: false`), so enabling ssl gives no mitm protection for the decrypted db credentials

packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::tls certificate verification permanently disabled for datasource connections (`rejectunauthorized: false`), so "ssl enabled" gives no mitm protection for credentials or query data

packages/backend/src/datasource/sql-validator.ts::select-only guard is bypassable: the validator inspects a comment-stripped copy while executequery concatenates and runs the original query text, allowing arbitrary multi-statement sql (delete/drop/set) on the connected datasource

packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::sql statement injection: validateselectquery validates a comment-stripped copy of the query, but executequery interpolates the original string into a simple-protocol query, so ddl/dml can be smuggled past the read-only guard

packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::select-only validator is bypassable: it validates a comment-stripped copy while executequery interpolates the original query text, enabling stacked-statement sql injection (drop/insert/etc.)

packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::raw-text oid guard is bypassed for array/range date-time types, so the timezone-shift bug it fixes still occurs for `timestamp[]`, `date[]`, `timestamptz[]`, `tsrange`, `tstzrange`

packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::partial/inconsistent fix for value fidelity: only date/timestamp/timestamptz are pinned to raw postgres text, while other pg types that the default parser turns into js objects still flow through and end up json-stringified into sheet cells. the change's own e2e expectations enshrine this: bytea renders as `{"type":"buffer","data":[222,173,190,239]}`, interval as `{"years":1,"months":2,"days":3}`, circle as `{"x":1,"y":2,"radius":3}`. if the intent is "cells show the value the database shows", these are user-visible wrong values left unaddressed; if the intent is only the timezone shift, the accepted json-blob rendering should be a stated decision (in the design doc) rather than an incidental test expectation.
